partners.mechanism_chain: Carbonic Anhydrase 12 (CA12) (HGNC:1320) —DISRUPTS→ Epithelial Ion Transport (GO:0007275); Epithelial Ion Transport (GO:0007275) —LEADS_TO→ Isolated hyperchlorhidrosis (MONDO:0007747); Carbonic Anhydrase 5A (CA5A) (HGNC:1324) —DISRUPTS→ Urea Cycle and Metabolism (GO:0006096); Urea Cycle and Metabolism (GO:0006096) —DECREASES→ Bicarbonate (CHEBI:15378); Bicarbonate (CHEBI:15378) —BINDS→ Epithelial Ion Transport (GO:0007275); Bicarbonate (CHEBI:15378) —LEADS_TO→ Hyperammonemic encephalopathy (MONDO:0014332). Loss-of-function mutations in CA12 disrupt epithelial ion transport, leading to hyperchlorhidrosis. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in CA5A disrupt the urea cycle, decreasing bicarbonate levels which are essential for proper neuronal function and ammonia detoxification, leading to hyperammonemic encephalopathy. ### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. autosomal recessive osteopetrosis 3  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.443)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-1475029)

**Proposed mechanism:** Loss-of-function variant in CA2 (rs373720231) —DISRUPTS→ Carbonic Anhydrase II (HGNC:1361); Carbonic Anhydrase II (HGNC:1361) —DECREASES→ Renal tubular acid-base homeostasis (GO:0001978); Renal tubular acid-base homeostasis (GO:0001978) —DECREASES→ Bicarbonate (CHEBI:16934); Bicarbonate (CHEBI:16934) —LEADS_TO→ Isolated hyperchlorhidrosis (HP:0000113); Carbonic Anhydrase II (HGNC:1361) —DECREASES→ Bone resorption (GO:0001574); Bone resorption (GO:0001574) —LEADS_TO→ Autosomal recessive osteopetrosis 3 (HP:0004574). Loss-of-function variants in Carbonic Anhydrase II (CA2) disrupt its enzymatic activity. In the kidney, this impairs the reabsorption of bicarbonate and subsequent secretion of hydrogen ions, leading to hyperchlorhidrosis. In osteoclasts, CA2 is crucial for generating the acidic environment required for bone resorption; its dysfunction leads to impaired bone resorption and osteopetrosis.

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in CA2 associated with isolated hyperchlorhidrosis or autosomal recessive osteopetrosis 3 with a population frequency >1% in gnomAD would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: rs373720231)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of Carbonic Anhydrase II in these distinct diseases could reveal novel therapeutic targets for managing both conditions. Strategies aimed at modulating CA2 activity or compensating for its loss could offer a unified approach.

#### 2. hyperammonemic encephalopathy due to carbonic anhydrase VA deficiency  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.401)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-1475029)

**Proposed mechanism:** Carbonic Anhydrase 12 (CA12) (HGNC:1320) —DISRUPTS→ Epithelial Ion Transport (GO:0007275); Epithelial Ion Transport (GO:0007275) —LEADS_TO→ Isolated hyperchlorhidrosis (MONDO:0007747); Carbonic Anhydrase 5A (CA5A) (HGNC:1324) —DISRUPTS→ Urea Cycle and Metabolism (GO:0006096); Urea Cycle and Metabolism (GO:0006096) —DECREASES→ Bicarbonate (CHEBI:15378); Bicarbonate (CHEBI:15378) —BINDS→ Epithelial Ion Transport (GO:0007275); Bicarbonate (CHEBI:15378) —LEADS_TO→ Hyperammonemic encephalopathy (MONDO:0014332). Loss-of-function mutations in CA12 disrupt epithelial ion transport, leading to hyperchlorhidrosis. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in CA5A disrupt the urea cycle, decreasing bicarbonate levels which are essential for proper neuronal function and ammonia detoxification, leading to hyperammonemic encephalopathy. The convergence is on bicarbonate's dual role in both epithelial transport and neuronal acid-base homeostasis.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that CA12 and CA5A do not functionally interact or converge on bicarbonate homeostasis in relevant tissues. _(variant: Presence of common variants (AF > 0.01) in gnomAD in the coding regions of CA12 or CA5A that are not associated with either phenotype.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of carbonic anhydrase activity in maintaining bicarbonate homeostasis across different physiological systems could lead to novel therapeutic strategies targeting interconnected pathways for managing these distinct rare diseases.
